messages:
samir: heads-up: vault audit delivery for namespace 'billing' stopped at ~02:07 UTC after an RBAC prune. we're missing ~18m of events. anyone on call see this?

ella: i removed some old CI bindings at 02:05 during the tidy. could be related. which SA is the sink writer?

secops-bot: Recent change: role=ci-audit-writer REMOVED from serviceAccount:svc-ci@redwood-project at 02:05:12 UTC by ella. Last successful sink write: 2026-04-12T02:06:58Z.

samir: that matches. audit sink wrote to gs://redwood-audit-processed/billing/. We have wrapped backups in gs://redwood-audit-backups/billing/*.enc. Need to rehydrate and import.

grant: quick question: who can decrypt with the evidence KMS key? kms-keeper or a human? prefer human decrypt for chain-of-custody.

kms-keeper: Key bindings: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter -> group:secops, serviceAccount:kms-importer@infra (was removed in RBAC sweep). Last change: RBAC-prune-2026-04-12 by ella.

ella: i didn't intend to remove the importer SA. i removed some stale accounts; looks like kms-importer lost decrypt. regrant request?

samir: options: (A) brief grant to kms-importer, decrypt+import automatically, then revoke OR (B) human decrypt under a secops account, import via vault CLI. I vote B for evidence chain.

grant: agreed. human decrypt. samir, i'll coordinate with secops to run gcloud decrypt on the wrapped blobs and upload plaintext to a sealed evidence bucket. please list object names.

samir: target blobs: billing-2026-04-12-02-06.enc .. billing-2026-04-12-02-24.enc (18 files). also compute sha256 of plaintext and store checksums.

secops-bot: Process checklist: 1) copy wrapped blobs to gs://secops-evidence/INC-2026-200/ 2) decrypt locally under authorized secops account 3) compute sha256 and upload plaintext to sealed bucket 4) run text-scan for secrets patterns and mark any matches for immediate rotation.

kms-keeper: Authorization: I'll approve a one-off manual decrypt by grant-holder grant (secops lead). Logging enabled.

grant: decrypt in progress. small snag: two wrapped objects return KMS error "DECRYPT_FAILED: ciphertext truncated". filenames: billing-02-12.enc, billing-02-17.enc.

samir: those truncated files could mean partial uploads. if they contain tokens we may not recover them. flag for forensic review.

vault-bot: audit-import dry-run: 102 events available, 2 files failed integrity checks (truncated). scan results: found 1 match: pattern "AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=[A-Z0-9]{20}" in billing-02-09.json.plain near line 24.

ell a: oh no. which key? do we have key id?

vault-bot: matched line: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIAEXAMPLE123456789, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY partially present in same file (truncated at column 42). Service: partner-s3-ingest. Last use recorded 02:09:12 UTC.

grant: treat as exposed. immediate actions: 1) disable the AWS access key in IAM 2) create new IAM key, 3) update k8s secret and restart partner-s3-ingest 4) revoke any related tokens in vault if the same creds were minted.

ella: i'll disable the AWS key now. command: aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id AKIAEXAMPLE123456789 --status Inactive --user-name partner-ingest

secops-bot: Evidence stored: gs://secops-evidence/INC-2026-200/ (wrapped+plaintext) sha256s recorded. Access limited to secops group.

samir: rotation plan executed: created new AWS key, updated secret in k8s: `kubectl -n prod set secret generic partner-s3-creds --from-literal=aws_access_key_id=REDACTED_NEW --from-literal=aws_secret_access_key=REDACTED_NEW` then `kubectl rollout restart deploy/partner-s3-ingest -n prod`.

grant: also run a provider-side revoke for any tokens or sessions tied to the old key. ask partner to confirm they rotated their side if they pulled creds.

vault-bot: after manual plaintext import (non-dry-run): 100 events imported, 2 events dropped (truncated blobs).

samir: record: old aws key disabled, new creds in place, k8s rollout succeeded (status: completed). kms-importer perms still removed. we'll keep it that way.

ell a: follow-ups: (1) add a pre-RBAC-sweep check that verifies no operational SA that owns sinks/keys will be removed without an owner ack, (2) add backup integrity checks that fail CI if wrapped blobs are zero-length or smaller than expected, (3) detection alert for any plaintext-looking creds pushed to repos or storage.

grant: creating incident INC-2026-200 and assigning owners: samir (containment), ella (change rollback/process), grant (postmortem). uploading artifacts and timeline. link: https://internal.redwood/incident/INC-2026-200

secops-bot: Actions completed: evidence sealed, exposed AWS key disabled, partner creds rotated, plaintext import counts reconciled. Remaining: postmortem write-up and RBAC workflow change.

samir: closing the loop here. thanks all. please add any additional artifacts to the incident doc before EOD. :thumbsup:
